model.rationale: This Atlanta-area seat leans heavily Democratic, and incumbent Hank Johnson is running again with a solid financial cushion while challenger James Duffie shows no reported fundraising. Markets price a Democratic win at roughly 98%, consistent with the fundamentals.
model.watch: A major polling surprise or unexpected outside spending against Johnson would be the main signal to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 4th District is a heavily Democratic, Atlanta-area seat with a partisan lean of D+27. Incumbent Hank Johnson, first elected in 2006, is seeking another term and has raised about $400,000 with roughly $118,000 on hand. Republican James Duffie reports no fundraising figures, leaving him at a steep resource disadvantage.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and incumbency. Prediction markets put Johnson's chances near 98%. The combination of a deep-blue electorate, an established incumbent, and an underfunded challenger makes this a Safe Democratic seat with little realistic path for an upset.
